candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — digoxin safety monitoring
candidate.educational_objective: Prioritize heart-rate assessment before digoxin administration and use individualized hold parameters because of bradycardia/conduction risk.

options.A: Assess the apical heart rate and follow the prescribed or facility hold parameters for bradycardia
options.B: Measure oral temperature and automatically hold the dose whenever the temperature exceeds 38 C
options.C: Measure respiratory rate and automatically hold the dose whenever it falls below 16 breaths/min
options.D: Check blood pressure only and administer digoxin without considering the client's heart rate

candidate.rationale: Digoxin slows heart rate and conduction and can cause clinically important bradycardia or heart block. NCBI nursing pharmacology guidance directs assessment of the apical heart rate before administration, while current DailyMed labeling confirms the bradycardia and conduction risks. The nurse should use the patient's prescribed/facility hold parameters rather than invent a universal cutoff. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Nursing guidance directs apical heart-rate assessment before digoxin; official labeling confirms digoxin can cause severe sinus bradycardia, sinoatrial block, and advanced/complete heart block in susceptible patients.
candidate.source_document_title: Nursing Pharmacology, 2nd ed., Chapter 6 Cardiac Glycosides; Digoxin Tablets official labeling
candidate.source_locator: Open RN Chapter 6.7 and Table 6.7a — assess apical heart rate; DailyMed Warnings and Precautions 5.2 — sinus bradycardia/sinoatrial block
candidate.source_organization: NCBI Bookshelf / Open RN; DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine
candidate.source_version_date: Open RN 2nd ed. 2023; current DailyMed label accessed 2026-08-17
candidate.stem: Before administering a scheduled oral dose of digoxin to an adult client, which assessment is most directly relevant to immediate medication safety?
